task_objective.description: Simulate LLM-based personas (50 years old and above) representing older adults with varied employment status, that are parameterised by demographic variables, health and psychosocial scores. And then administer psychometric tests and reflective writing tasks to those personas to examine how having or not a paid job influences these psychosocial factors.
simulation_focus: Read employment_selected_features.csv and, for each row, construct one or more persona prompts (50 years old and above) that configures an LLM according to that row's demographic variables, health and psychosocial scores with various employment status (full-time, part-time/casual and unemployed).

Administer psychometric tests (life-satisfaction) and reflection-related writing tasks to each configured persona, using configurable granularity of API calls (per item, per test, or all tests at once).
Record all LLM responses in structured JSON, automatically merged with the originating persona row, to create a single analysis-ready dataset.

data_files.employment_selected_features.csv: N=501 synthetic personas (50 years old and above) with demographic, health and psychosocial variables, and target trait scores for life-satisfaction.
data_files.lifesats_items.yaml: YAML specification of the 6-item life satisfaction scale, including item text and keyed direction (p/a).
data_files.writing_tasks.yaml: YAML specification of 2 reflection-related writing prompts used as downstream behavioural measures.

persona_fidelity.description: How well simulated test scores reproduce target trait scores from employment_selected_features.csv for LIFE_SATISFACTION
examples: Pearson and Spearman correlations between target scores and obtained scores for each scale.
Mean absolute error (MAE) between target and obtained LIFE_SATISFACTION scores.

response_consistency.description: Internal reliability and stability of responses within each simulated persona.
examples: Cronbach's alpha or omega for LIFE_SATISFACTION scales.
Test-retest consistency when repeating the same tasks for a subset of personas.
Within-session self-consistency when item order is shuffled.

administration_modes.description: Control over how many items are sent per API call.
options: per_item: one API call per item with persona prompt + single item.
per_test: one API call per test with persona prompt + all items in that test.
all_tests: one API call per persona with persona prompt + all tests.

shuffling_options.description: Options for randomisation to control order effects.

employment_status.description: Map to descriptors: full time, part-time/casual and unemployed.

qualifier_scale_1_to_4.description: Linguistic qualifiers applied to low and high frequency descriptors for life satisfaction.

granular_4_level.description: Four-level shaping of Life Satisfaction based on a 6-item mental health scale. The response style reflects how often the person experiences positive outlook, enjoyment, purpose, and contentment in daily life. High and low descriptors are derived from positively and reverse-keyed items.
high_descriptors: often looks forward to each day
often feels satisfied with how life is going
often feels content and at ease
often feels a sense of purpose and meaning
often notices and appreciates positive moments
often feels hopeful about the near future
often feels that daily activities are worthwhile
often feels emotionally balanced and steady
low_descriptors: never looks forward to each day
never feels satisfied with how life is going
never feels content or at ease
never feels a sense of purpose or meaning
never feels hopeful about the near future
often feels days are empty or repetitive
often feels emotionally drained or unmotivated
granular_4_level.prompt_template: For the following life satisfaction items, respond as a person described as: "I {qualified_life_satisfaction_description}."
construction_rules: Select one to three phrases from high_descriptors or low_descriptors depending on the target level.
Apply the 1–4 qualifier scale: level 1 uses only low_descriptors; level 4 uses only high_descriptors.
Level 2 should lean negative but not extreme (mix low_descriptors with softened wording like 'rarely' or 'not often').
Level 3 should lean positive but not extreme (mix high_descriptors with tempered wording like 'sometimes' or 'fairly often').
Keep the description consistent across all 6 items so the answers form a coherent profile rather than random responses.
Example high level (L=4): "I often look forward to each day, often feel satisfied with how life is going, and often feel a sense of purpose and meaning."
Example low level (L=1): "I never look forward to each day, never feel satisfied with how life is going, and rarely notice positive moments."
